about.heading: About Us
about.imageAlt: Murti of Shri Durga Mata — Navyuvak Durga Utsav Mandal
about.intro: Established in 1980, our Navyuvak Durga Utsav Mandal celebrates a grand Navratri festival for Shri Durga Mata every year in the sacred courtyard of Shri Shiv Mandir Maruti Devasthan, Zingabai Takli, Zenda Chowk.
about.history: For over four decades we have carried forward a legacy of devotion, culture and community unity. Through nine days of celebration, we organize daily aarti-bhajan, vibrant garba-dandiya, cultural programs and a grand mahaprasad, filling the entire area with a devotional atmosphere.
about.mission: Bringing together the energy of the youth and the experience of our elders, our mandal reaches new heights every year — and it is only with the support of all of you that this festival keeps growing grander.
about.jyotImageAlt: Akhand Manokamna Jyot and Ghatasthapana — Navyuvak Durga Utsav Mandal
about.jyotInfo: Every year, the mandal lights an eternal sacred flame (Akhand Manokamna Jyot) at the feet of Shri Durga Mata — burning continuously for nine days as a symbol of fulfilling devotees' wishes. Devotees from Zingabai Takli and the surrounding area faithfully register their ghat. On the auspicious day of Ghatasthapana, all registered devotees are specially invited, and after a formal puja, the flame is lit by their own sacred hands — a moment that connects every devotee directly to the Goddess's grace.
about.jyotSource: Navratri 2026 — the flame is brought from Shri Renuka Devi Mandir, Mahurgad, Nanded
about.aartiTime: 8:05 in the morning and 8:05 in the evening

durga.heading: Shri Durga Mata
durga.name: Shri Durga Mata
durga.intro: Jagadamba, the radiant form of the primal cosmic power — who destroys evil and protects the virtuous. During this sacred festival of Navratri, the form of Shri Durga Mata is a feast for the eyes; witnessing the divine glow and gracious gaze on her face fills every devotee's heart with devotion. Bowing at the Goddess's feet dispels fear and worry from the mind, bringing a renewed sense of energy and faith.
durga.significance: Over the nine days of Navratri, the Goddess's nine forms — Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri and Siddhidatri — are worshipped in proper ritual order. Each day carries its own significance, color and devotional spirit, filling the whole area with aarti, bhajans and chanting.
durga.darshan: The grand and enchanting darshan of Shri Durga Mata at the mandap is open free of charge to all devotees. Darshan and mahaprasad are provided to everyone in an organized, hassle-free manner.
